title: Jerusalem artichoke, apple and egg traybake

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a whole food or plain staple: artichokes, onions, apples, kale, eggs, tinned butter beans, olive oil and bread.

supermarket.reason: Tesco stocks Jerusalem artichokes in November, and everything else is an everyday item at an ordinary price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large roasting tray and a knife, and cracking eggs into gaps is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 600g artichokes, two eggs each, a tin of beans and bread make a fair meal for four, and roasting at 200°C for about 45 minutes in stages should leave the artichokes tender and the egg whites set.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for scrubbing and halving the artichokes and cutting the onions, apples and kale, and the 25, 10 and 8 to 10 minute roasting stages add up to the 45 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the sage, salt and pepper, appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot roasted traybake built on Jerusalem artichokes suits a November evening, and the artichokes are the main part of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, butter beans, roasted roots, kale and apple with bread make a filling, balanced family dinner.
